classification.difficultyReason: Read amplitude and period from transformed trigonometric rules and sketch their graphs on a specified radian interval.

content.prompt: State the amplitude and period of each function, then sketch its graph for $[-\pi,\pi]$.

answer.short: Amplitude $3$; period $\pi$. Maxima at $(-\pi,3)$, $(0,3)$ and $(\pi,3)$; minima at $(-\frac{\pi}{2},-3)$ and $(\frac{\pi}{2},-3)$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Amplitude}&=|3|=3\\T&=\frac{2\pi}{2}=\pi\end{aligned}$$
Horizontally dilate $y=\cos x$ by factor $\tfrac12$, then vertically dilate by factor $3$. Over $[-\pi,\pi]$, sketch two cycles with maxima at $x=-\pi,0,\pi$ and minima at $x=\pm\tfrac\pi2$. The zeros are $x=\pm\tfrac\pi4,\pm\tfrac{3\pi}4$.

answer.short: Amplitude $2$; period $4\pi$. The graph increases from $(-\pi,-2)$ through $(0,0)$ to $(\pi,2)$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Amplitude}&=|2|=2\\T&=\frac{2\pi}{1/2}=4\pi\end{aligned}$$
Horizontally dilate $y=\sin x$ by factor $2$, then vertically dilate by factor $2$. The interval $[-\pi,\pi]$ shows half a cycle, increasing from $(-\pi,-2)$ through $(0,0)$ to $(\pi,2)$.

answer.short: Amplitude is not defined; period $\tfrac{2\pi}{3}$. Zeros at $x=-\tfrac{2\pi}{3},0,\tfrac{2\pi}{3}$; vertical asymptotes at $x=-\pi,-\tfrac\pi3,\tfrac\pi3,\pi$.
answer.worked:
Tangent has no amplitude because it is unbounded.
$$\begin{aligned}T&=\frac{\pi}{3/2}=\frac{2\pi}{3}\end{aligned}$$
Horizontally dilate $y=\tan x$ by factor $\tfrac23$. The zeros satisfy $\tfrac{3x}{2}=n\pi$, giving $x=-\tfrac{2\pi}{3},0,\tfrac{2\pi}{3}$ in the interval. Vertical asymptotes satisfy $\tfrac{3x}{2}=\tfrac\pi2+n\pi$, giving $x=-\pi,-\tfrac\pi3,\tfrac\pi3,\pi$. Draw an increasing branch between each adjacent pair of asymptotes; the function is undefined at the domain endpoints.

answer.short: Amplitude $2$; period $\tfrac{2\pi}{3}$. Maxima at $x=-\tfrac{2\pi}{3},0,\tfrac{2\pi}{3}$ have value $2$; minima at $x=-\pi,-\tfrac\pi3,\tfrac\pi3,\pi$ have value $-2$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Amplitude}&=|2|=2\\T&=\frac{2\pi}{3}\end{aligned}$$
Horizontally dilate $y=\cos x$ by factor $\tfrac13$, then vertically dilate by factor $2$. Sketch three cycles over $[-\pi,\pi]$. Maxima occur at $x=-\tfrac{2\pi}{3},0,\tfrac{2\pi}{3}$ and minima at $x=-\pi,-\tfrac\pi3,\tfrac\pi3,\pi$. The zeros are $x=\pm\tfrac\pi6,\pm\tfrac\pi2,\pm\tfrac{5\pi}6$.
